title: Сколько денег нужно  (How Much Money Does It Take)

segments.t: In our last scene, Nina finally accepted young Ivan's proposal outside the registry office. Now the show's satirical opening credits roll, featuring a catchy and ironic ballad about the insatiable greed of Russian officials who steal millions while dreaming of villas in Monaco and offshore accounts in Switzerland. Let's listen to the opening song in Russian first; don't worry about catching every word.
Сколько денег нужно, чтобы стать счастливым?
И вот уже есть миллионов шесть!
Вилла в Монако, в Швейцарии счёт.
На кухне картины Дали и Ван Гога.
Now let's examine the satirical lyrics of the opening theme song line by line. The opening animation shows a corrupt mayor dreaming of luxury yachts.
Сколько денег нужно, чтобы стать счастливым?
'How much money does it take to be happy?' The opening rhetorical question sets the satirical tone of the series.
'How much money do you need?' Notice the dative pronoun indicating the person who needs the money.
'A little bit there, a little bit here.' The rhyming adverbs describe accumulating wealth through petty bribes.
И вот уже есть миллионов шесть!
'And just like that, you've got six million!' The genitive plural noun follows the cardinal numeral for 'six'.
Вилла в Монако, в Швейцарии счёт.
'A villa in Monaco, an account in Switzerland.' The lyrics list typical status symbols of corrupt officials.
'But you need, need, need even more!' The comparative adverb emphasizes the theme of bottomless greed.
'A supermodel wife and a mistress too.' The narrator lists the corrupt official's domestic luxuries.
'Only she's just a little bit younger!' The comparative adjective with a prefix means 'somewhat younger'.
'A white yacht sails across the sea.' A classic image of luxury sailing on the Mediterranean.
'Happiness is getting closer, almost here!' The adverbial idiom expresses an imminent arrival.
На кухне картины Дали и Ван Гога.
'Paintings by Dali and Van Gogh in the kitchen.' Prepositional plural forms describe opulent wall decor.
'A church, a mosque, and a synagogue are built.' Short passive participle describing lavish religious donations.
'And for insurance, a Buddhist temple too!' The noun phrase explains superstitious hedge investments.
'If it doesn't pan out here, it will pan out there!' The colloquial idiom means 'to succeed or work out'. Now let's listen to the entire opening song again without interruption.
Сколько денег нужно, чтобы стать счастливым?
И вот уже есть миллионов шесть!
Вилла в Монако, в Швейцарии счёт.
На кухне картины Дали и Ван Гога.
The opening credits capture the endless greed driving the plot of the series. In the next scene, we return to the present day where Samsonov fumes over Nina's vacation photos.
